title: Scoped Invite Policies and Org-level Email Allowlist for SSO-enabled Tenants
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Add first-class org-level invite controls that let admins define scoped invite policies (invite by role, team scoping) and enforce email allowlists/denylist semantics across orgs — with special behavior for SSO/SAML-enforced tenants. This ticket implements backend APIs, console UX, RBAC v2 policy hooks, and audit-log events needed for compliance teams.

Scope includes:
- API: PUT/GET org invite policy object (fields: allowlist_domains, denylist_addresses, allowed_roles_on_invite, require_admin_approval_for_external_invites, invite_expiry_days)
- Console: Admin settings page to configure allowlist/denylist, preview effective policy for teams, and bulk-validate pending invites
- SSO behavior: For orgs with SAML enabled & "SSO enforced", allowlist is used only for non-SAML invites; optionally block email invites entirely unless allowed_by_idp is true.
- RBAC integration: Enforce allowed_roles_on_invite to prevent non-admins from inviting users into high-privilege roles. Hooks added to invite flow and to API endpoints used by infra (SCIM / provisioning).
- Audit: Emit granular audit events for policy changes, blocked invites, admin overrides, and bulk imports. Events must include actor, target email, rule matched, and prior policy id.
- Migration: Provide safe default for existing orgs (no blocking), and a migration tester to preview blocked users before enforcement.

Out of scope for this ticket: SSO IdP-managed attribute mapping UI, enterprise migration assistance (separate SOC project).
acceptance_criteria: Org admin can create/update invite policy via API and Console and see policy version metadata
Invite flow rejects/flags invites that violate allowlist/denylist and returns clear error codes/messages for SDK/API clients
RBAC prevents non-admin users from assigning roles not allowed by org policy when creating invites
Audit events emitted for policy changes and for each blocked invite; events searchable in Console logs
Feature respects SAML-enforced org behavior: when "SSO enforced" is true, email invites are blocked by default unless explicit override by admin
Migration path exists: admins can run a preview job that returns a list of currently pending or historical invites that would be blocked if policy enforced
implementation_notes: Schema: add org_invite_policies table with jsonb 'rules' and integer 'policy_version'
API: /v1/orgs/{org_id}/invite_policy (GET, PUT, PATCH). Request validation runs through common policy lib
Invite flow: centralize invite creation through invite_service; add policy check that returns (allowed|blocked|requires_admin_approval)
Audit: extend audit service with new event types: INVITE_POLICY_UPDATED, INVITE_BLOCKED, INVITE_ADMIN_OVERRIDE
SCIM/Provisioning: when provisioning via IdP, bypass invite checks if source == 'idp' and org.sso_enforced == true
Console: settings page wireframes in Confluence + 2 new API calls for bulk-validate and preview
Telemetry: add metrics (invites_blocked_total, policy_updates_total, overrides_total) and tag by org_id and rule_id
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): API + invite_service check behind feature flag for 5 internal orgs and Redwood testbed
Phase 2 (preview): UI + preview job enabled for selected customer beta orgs; collect feedback
Phase 3 (enforce opt-in): enable enforcement for orgs that opt-in via Console; provide migration report
Phase 4 (enforce opt-out): after 6 weeks, enable enforcement by default for new orgs and orgs with SSO enforced
Rollback: feature-flag off removes enforcement but keeps audit history; suppression of false positives via admin override endpoint
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False-positives blocking legitimate invites -> Mitigation: Provide preview report and admin-override endpoint; short TTL enforcement at start
Risk: SCIM/provisioning breakage for IdP flows -> Mitigation: explicitly bypass policy for idp-source and add integration tests with Okta/Azure
Risk: Audit volume spike -> Mitigation: sample non-fatal events and batch emission for high-volume orgs
